stories.headline: Lake City Man Arrested on Child Pornography Charges
stories.summary: Joshua Lee Hoger, 30, of Lake City was arrested Thursday after Columbia County Sheriff's Office detectives found over 20 images and videos of child sexual abuse material on his computer. The investigation began January 26 when the North Florida Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force received a tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. After tracing the case to a Lake City address and serving search warrants, authorities recovered evidence and issued an arrest warrant. Hoger was booked into the Columbia County Detention Facility on charges of using a two-way communication device to commit a felony and possession of child pornography. The investigation is ongoing and more charges could be filed.

stories.headline: Wildfire Response Ramps Up Across North Florida; Air Tankers Staged in Lake City
stories.summary: The Florida Forest Service has moved large air tankers to Lake City as wildfire response intensifies across North Florida. According to News4Jax, Jacksonville Fire Rescue has responded to 29 wildfire incidents so far this year — more than double the 13 from the same period last year. In Duval County alone, the Forest Service has gone from 1 fire on 1 acre at this point last year to 11 fires on 50 acres. Four tractor plow units are now dedicated to Duval County. Officials urge residents to clear vegetation away from homes, trim bushes and trees, rake leaves several feet from structures, and clean roofs and gutters since fire travels by air as well as by ground.

stories.headline: Two Arrested in Lake City Undercover Child Predator Operation; One Suspect From Fort White
stories.summary: Two men face charges after Lake City police conducted an undercover operation to catch online child predators. Joseph Anderson, 25, of Chiefland and Robert Smith, 38, of Fort White were arrested after attempting to arrange meetings with who they believed were underage girls — but were actually undercover detectives. Anderson was arrested Monday and Smith was taken into custody on Tuesday. Both men engaged in sexually explicit conversations before arranging the meetings, according to police.

stories.headline: Drought Worsens Across Northeast Florida Despite Sunday's Storms
stories.summary: Despite Sunday's severe weather, Northeast Florida's drought situation remains dire. According to News4Jax meteorologist Katie Garner, the region is sitting at 'severe drought' — just one step below 'extreme.' The storms on February 15 barely made a dent in the rainfall deficit. Fire risk remains elevated, with dry conditions making it easier for wildfires to start and spread. Light winds of 5–10 mph and mild temperatures around 69°F are expected early this week.

stories.headline: National Wildfire Prevention Team Deployed to Florida Amid Growing Fire Risk
stories.summary: The National Wildfire Prevention and Education team has arrived in Florida for a two-week assignment to raise awareness about wildfire risk as drought conditions worsen. According to the Florida Forest Service, human activity causes 80% of wildfires — including outdoor cooking, campfires, yard debris burning, and even sparks from vehicle maintenance issues like low tire pressure or towing chains. About 95% of Florida is experiencing at least moderate drought, with severe drought conditions across Central and North Florida. Residents are urged not to burn anything outdoors and to clear vegetation away from homes.

stories.headline: Severe Storms and Tornado Watch Hit Northeast Florida Sunday
stories.summary: A strong cold front brought severe storms across Northeast Florida on Sunday, February 15, prompting a tornado watch through 8 p.m. The Storm Prediction Center placed the region at a Level 2 (Slight Risk) for severe weather. A Wind Advisory was in effect for areas west of the St. Johns River as south winds gusted up to 35–45 mph. The main squall line moved through western counties between 2–3 p.m. and reached inland Northeast Florida counties including Baker, Bradford, Clay, and Alachua by 4–5 p.m. The threat diminished by late evening as the cold front pushed through.

stories.headline: 47th Annual Olustee Festival Draws Crowds to Lake City
stories.summary: Lake City hosted the 47th Annual Olustee Festival over Presidents' Day weekend at Wilson Park on Lake DeSoto, commemorating the 1864 Battle of Olustee — the largest Civil War engagement fought in Florida. The festival, held annually since 1976, featured over 150 vendors, food trucks, a children's area, local entertainment, and homemade arts and crafts from across the country. Road closures were in effect around downtown Lake City. The festival ran Friday and Saturday, February 13–14, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

stories.headline: Wildfires Surge Across Florida as Drought Reaches 25-Year High
stories.summary: Florida is experiencing its worst drought in 25 years, with the Florida Forest Service reporting more than 650 wildfires and over 21,000 acres burned since January 1, 2026. According to Fox Weather, 98% of the state is under some level of drought, with 85% in severe drought — the most since March 2001. Emergency burn bans are active in 34 of 67 counties, including Columbia County. A wildfire in Marion County forced the closure of State Road 19 between CR-314 and SR-40, with detours in place.

stories.headline: Gov. DeSantis Declares State of Emergency Over Drought and Cold Weather
stories.summary: Governor Ron DeSantis signed Executive Order 26-33 on Monday, February 9 declaring a state of emergency due to worsening drought and the impact of recent cold weather on Florida agriculture. The order provides emergency support for farmers, waives agricultural weight restrictions for crop transport, and directs the state to seek federal aid from the USDA and Small Business Administration. The Suwannee River Water Management District, which includes Columbia County, has an ongoing water shortage advisory citing an average rainfall deficit of nearly 11.5 inches across 14 of its 15 counties.

stories.headline: Rep. Cammack Hosts Farm Bill Listening Session at Santa Fe River Ranch
stories.summary: Congresswoman Kat Cammack hosted an agricultural listening session on Friday, February 13 at the Santa Fe River Ranch in North Central Florida, hours before a draft of the 2026 Farm Bill was released. Cammack highlighted wins including long-term funding to combat Citrus Greening disease, increased block grants for Florida farmers, and specialty crop innovation. She also noted additional disaster relief funding is on the way for farmers impacted by tariffs and recent freezing temperatures, and pushed for the expansion of broadband and water infrastructure in rural communities.

stories.headline: 49th Annual Battle of Olustee Re-enactment Wraps Up
stories.summary: The 49th Annual Battle of Olustee Re-enactment, the largest Civil War re-enactment in Florida and one of the largest in the Southeast, concluded Sunday, February 15 at Olustee Battlefield Historic State Park on US-90 east of Lake City. The three-day event running February 13–15 featured living history camps, period demonstrations, and the main battle re-enactment. The original 1864 battle involved 10,000 troops and was the largest Civil War engagement in Florida, with three U.S. Colored Regiments taking part including the 54th Massachusetts, later immortalized in the film Glory.

stories.headline: Florida Burn Bans Expand as Drought Intensifies Statewide
stories.summary: Counties across Florida, including Columbia County, continue under burn bans as drought conditions worsen. According to WUFT, 100% of the state is now experiencing some form of drought, with extreme drought (Level 4 of 5) covering 43% of Florida — nearly double from the prior week. Severe drought (Level 3) covers over 85% of the state. Residents are urged to avoid all open burning and conserve water. The long-term outlook indicates below-average rainfall over the next three months.

stories.headline: High-Speed Chase Ends with K-9 Apprehension in Columbia County
stories.summary: On the night of February 10, a deputy working traffic enforcement near CR 131 and SW Cumorah Hill attempted to stop a silver Chevrolet Traverse that ran a stop sign. The driver, Jeffery Allen Steele, 44, of Wellborn, accelerated to 102 mph. Deputies deployed spike strips and performed a P.I.T. maneuver to stop the vehicle south of CR-242A. After Steele refused to exit, a K-9 was deployed. Deputies found multiple narcotics and drug paraphernalia. Steele was booked into the Columbia County Detention Facility on $32,000 bond.

stories.headline: Columbia County Commissioners Weigh In on Fort White Dissolution Proposal
stories.summary: Columbia County commissioners expressed concerns on Thursday, February 5 about the possibility of the town of Fort White dissolving. Commissioner Rocky Ford was adamant the county needs to be more involved in the process. However, commissioners ultimately cannot control whether or not the town dissolves. The discussion follows months of tense town council meetings, including Mayor George Thomas walking out during a December meeting amid a decorum debate. The next Fort White town council meeting is set for Tuesday, February 17.

stories.headline: Columbia County Approves Emergency Burn Ban Amid Wildfire Risk
stories.summary: Columbia County commissioners called an emergency meeting on Thursday, February 5 to approve a temporary county-wide burn ban at the request of the Florida Forest Service. Commission chair Tim Murphy said the Forest Service warned about an increase in fires across the region and ongoing drought conditions. Surrounding counties including Alachua, Union, Bradford, Gilchrist, and Putnam had already enacted similar bans. The burn ban restricts all open burning and will be reviewed every ten days.
